definition: The task of identifying inputs that differ significantly from the distribution of data a model was trained on, so the system can flag uncertainty or defer to a human.
details: OOD detection is important for safe deployment, helping systems recognize when they are being asked to operate outside their reliable competence and should respond with caution or abstain.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. Boil it down and it is this: The task of identifying inputs that differ significantly from the distribution of data a model was trained on, so the system can flag uncertainty or defer to a human. Here is why it matters: OOD detection is important for safe deployment, helping systems recognize when they are being asked to operate outside their reliable competence and should respond with caution or abstain. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. That deliberate caution is Out-of-Distribution Detection.
